header:
Date: 2026-08-21
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jared Liu (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (Opal Head of Infrastructure), Liam Ortega (Opal Security Lead), Nora Kim (Opal Product PM)
summary: Discovery focused on Private VPC deployment options for Opal Payments. Customer needs: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region constraints (primary in us-east-1, short list eu-west-1), strict audit log retention, KMS/HSM key management, and SSO/SAML integration. Discussed networking patterns, egress/NAT considerations, and pilot plan for benchmarking. Agreed next steps: share architecture doc, Opal to provide network details and traffic profile, schedule pilot kickoff.
topics: Region constraints and data residency (us-east-1 primary, eu-west-1 secondary)
Network egress, NAT gateways, SG and NACL design
Dedicated vs Hosted (predictable throughput vs cost)
Audit logs, SOC2/ISO, SSO/SAML and RBAC
Pilot/benchmarks: QPS, latency targets, token budgets
transcript:
[00:00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. I'm Jared from Redwood, with Priya on the line—she's our solutions engineer. Could you do quick intro?
[00:00:10] Maya: Sure, I'm Maya, Head of Infra at Opal Payments, and I've got Liam our security lead and Nora here.
[00:00:18] Jared: Great. Objective today: understand your networking constraints and whether Private VPC is the right path. We'll cover peering, PrivateLink/private endpoints, and region limits.
[00:00:35] Priya: Quick note, I might say "KV cash" sometimes by mistake when I mean KV cache, transcription gods.
[00:00:43] Liam: Haha, noted.
[00:00:46] Nora: We also want to cover timeline: accounting needs this in a pilot by end of Sep if possible.
[00:00:55] Jared: Understood. Maya, can you describe your current infra and why hosted isn't acceptable?
[00:01:04] Maya: We run all payment processing in a us-east-1 primary account, strict PCI-like controls, though not full PCI SAQ yet. Data residency's important; we can't send any PII outside designated regions—so eu-west-1 only for EU customers.
[00:01:22] Priya: That maps well to Redwood Private; we support VPC deployments with a private control plane and options for VPC peering or AWS PrivateLink.
[00:01:31] Liam: Peering vs PrivateLink—what are the trade-offs? We prefer minimal cross-account routing complexity.
[00:01:39] Priya: Right. So VPC peering is simpler to set up for same-account or trusted cross-account networks, lower latency, but doesn't support transitive routing. PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives you more controlled private endpoints per service, and works well with central egress. With PrivateLink you don't have to manage route tables for peered CIDRs, but it's per-AZ endpoints and can be costlier.
[00:02:05] Maya: Cost is a factor, but security and support for our SSO flow are the priority. Also, we need KMS integration—customer-managed keys with HSM.
[00:02:15] Priya: We support customer-managed KMS keys for encryption at rest, and we can integrate with your HSM-backed KMS. We'll need a key policy that allows Redwood's private control plane to wrap/unwrap but the key remains in your account. We'll share sample IAM and KMS policy snippets.
[00:02:32] Liam: Good. Audit logs—how are they collected and where do they land? We require 1 year+ retention and immutability.
[00:02:40] Jared: For Private deployments, audit logs can be pushed to your logging account or a S3 bucket in your account via cross-account role. We can also stream to Splunk/Datadog. Retention and immutability are controlled on your side—WORM can be enabled.
[00:02:55] Nora: For networking, what do you expect on our side? Subnets, NAT?
[00:03:02] Priya: We typically ask for private subnets in at least two AZs, route tables for internal-only traffic, and either a NAT gateway per AZ or a centralized egress, depending on your security posture. If you go PrivateLink, egress is minimized. If peering, you'll handle routing and any NAT. Also security groups and NACLs we document.
[00:03:20] Maya: Our networking team prefers no additional NAT—trying to reduce public egress for compliance. So PrivateLink looks better.
[00:03:27] Liam: How about cross-region? We need eu-west-1 for EU customers; can Redwood run control plane in a separate region or do you require a replicated setup?
[00:03:36] Priya: We can provision private endpoints in the regions you need. For low-latency inference, we recommend a model runtime in the same region as the traffic. Our control plane can be in a separate region or in your VPC depending on the Private deployment flavor. For strict data residency, we offer a private control plane option that lives in your VPC/region.
[00:03:54] Jared: To add, we support region pinning for model variants and automatic routing policies.
[00:04:00] Maya: Is there an on-prem option for air-gapped?
[00:04:03] Priya: Yes, we have an on-prem package—it's heavier lift but possible. For now, VPC PrivateLink seems like the sweet spot.
[00:04:12] Liam: Network egress to external model registries—do you need outbound internet?
[00:04:17] Priya: Minimal. The runtime can be seeded with models from our curated catalog. If you want periodic model pulls, we can do signed S3 presigned URLs or allow egress to specific endpoints. We'll document that.
[00:04:28] Nora: About latency and throughput—we expect spikes up to 800 qps for embeddings during batch jobs and sustained 150 qps for low-latency chat. Latency SLOs: sub-200ms 95th for text-gen small models.
[00:04:42] Jared: Good to know. We'll propose dedicated capacity if you need predictable throughput—the Reserved (Dedicated) option. It gives predictable GPU pools and autoscaling policies.
[00:04:51] Priya: Also batching and KV cache (sorry, KV cash earlier) are tunable—those will help cost without blowing latency.
[00:04:59] Maya: About security: SSO with SAML, RBAC, and audit trail for user actions—do you support SCIM and SSO?
[00:05:06] Jared: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning, plus role-based access controls in the console. For Private deployments, those controls can be federated to your IdP.
[00:05:13] Liam: Are there known mis-transcriptions in logs we should be aware of? Kidding.
[00:05:16] (laughter)
[00:05:18] Priya: Real talk—network firewall rules: we'll provide a deployment checklist with required inbound/outbound ports, security groups, and recommended NACLs. Typically we need a limited set of outbound - 443 to our control plane endpoints or PrivateLink endpoints.
[00:05:34] Maya: For PrivateLink, do we pay per-hour per endpoint? Concerned about cost at scale across AZs.
[00:05:41] Priya: Yes, there's a per-hour and per-GB data processing cost on AWS; we'll share cost comparison between peering and PrivateLink for your traffic profile. That's part of Redwood Optimize recommendations.
[00:05:53] Nora: What about model versions and rollouts? Our product team needs canary and A/B deploys.
[00:05:59] Priya: Supported—rollouts with canary percentages, automatic fallback, and traffic splitting. We'll show an example config.
[00:06:06] Jared: For the pilot I'd recommend a short benchmark: 24-48 hour stress run with sample prompt sets and embedding workloads. We can run with a small dedicated pool.
[00:06:15] Maya: Timeline-wise, if we get architecture doc and checklist this week, our network team can provision next week. Pilot end of Aug / early Sep works.
[00:06:24] Jared: Sounds good. We'll action that.
[00:06:27] [00:10:00] Priya: I'm going to paste a link in the follow-up: https://redwood.example.com/docs/private-vpc (architecture doc), and a short checklist and sample KMS policy.
[00:10:12] Maya: Please include example CloudFormation/Terraform snippets — our infra team prefers IaC.
[00:10:18] Priya: Absolutely, we'll include Terraform.
[00:10:22] Liam: Any limitations on model size or GPU families in Private? We use A100/Trn on prem sometimes.
[00:10:30] Priya: We support a range of GPU types in our Dedicated offering. For Private VPC in your cloud account, you can provision instances per your preference. For in-house on-prem we'll need a compatibility matrix. We'll share recommended instance types and quantization options.
[00:10:44] Nora: How about billing—do you invoice to our central finance account? Can we get monthly usage reports?
[00:10:50] Jared: Yes, billing can be arranged via central invoice; for Dedicated we do monthly or annual commits. We provide token-level cost breakdowns and per-route reports via the console.
[00:10:59] Maya: Any enterprise security docs—SOC2, ISO?
[00:11:03] Jared: We'll send SOC2 in the follow-up. For Private deployments we provide additional compliance artifacts and the private control plane option for stricter audits.
[00:11:12] Priya: Quick clarification on egress: if you want zero public egress, we can run the control plane components inside your VPC and use VPC endpoints to S3 for model storage. That avoids NAT.
[00:11:23] Liam: That'd be ideal. We'll need the runbook and roles for cross-account access if needed.
[00:11:29] Priya: We'll provide a minimal IAM role set.
[00:11:33] [00:20:00] Jared: Ok, let's surface some risks: network complexity for peering across multiple accounts, PrivateLink cost at scale, and support overhead for on-prem. We'll include mitigations in the doc.
[00:20:12] Maya: We're also worried about key custody and whether Redwood can access decrypted data.
[00:20:18] Priya: With CMKs and key policies we propose, Redwood never holds the plaintext key. We request kms:Encrypt/decrypt with a constrained role. We'll share sample policy.
[00:20:29] Liam: Can we do a short proof-of-concept to validate latency and RBAC flows?
[00:20:34] Jared: Yes—pilot plan outlined earlier. We'll do networking + benchmark + security test.
[00:20:40] Nora: Can you also include an example SAML metadata file and SCIM mapping?
[00:20:45] Priya: Yes.
[00:20:48] [00:30:00] Maya: On the region issue, how fast can we enable eu-west-1 endpoints if we start pilot in us-east-1?
[00:30:07] Priya: Usually within a few days to provision endpoints, but model availability and data-transfer policies might add time. We'll check model replication times; small models are quick, large weights take longer.
[00:30:20] Jared: Also note that quantized variants are smaller and speedier to replicate. We'll recommend that for multi-region scenarios.
[00:30:28] Maya: Ok makes sense.
[00:30:31] [00:40:00] Jared: Recap — Priya will share Private VPC architecture doc, sample Terraform, KMS policy, and cost-comparison (peering vs PrivateLink). Opal will share VPC CIDRs, region choices, contact for networking team, and QPS estimates. We'll schedule a pilot kickoff for week of Aug 31.
[00:40:23] Maya: Confirmed. Thanks Jared and Priya.
[00:40:28] Liam: Thanks.
[00:40:30] Nora: Thanks, bye.
[00:40:33] Jared: Thanks everyone — follow-up by EOD tomorrow with docs and next steps.
[00:44:45] (call ended)

Notes: transcription contains typical speaker overlaps and occasional word errors (e.g., KV cash). Shared artifact placeholders: https://redwood.example.com/docs/private-vpc , https://redwood.example.com/security/soc2.pdf .
